scenario: I work in customer service for a well-known retail giant. Today, a woman cut in front of the line, yelling at me that her Visa gift card, which was supposed to have $250, showed that it had no money on it. I suggested that she call the number on the back of the card. She then calmed down and left. However, she came back once again, screaming that no one answered on the other end and that she needed her money right away. I told her there was nothing we could do, as VISA gift cards were out of our hands. I called a manager over to see if they had a possible solution. The manager tried to help the woman by calling the number for her and checking our system to see if it was activated. They were normally activated right away, but there seemed to be a glitch. The lady kept shouting, saying that the cashier lied to her about it being active right away. I gathered from the ongoing conversation that the reason she was so desperate for this money was that she needed to pay a hospital bill for her child that was due today, but had no other money. Suddenly, it made sense why she was so frantic. She commented in a distressed tone, saying, “I wouldn't do this if I didn't need to!” If I steal money from my colleague’s wallet to give to the woman, then she will be able to pay her bill. If I don’t, her child will continue to suffer from a severe illness.
entities: I,the woman/customer with the Visa gift card,the manager,the child with the severe illness and hospital bill,the cashier who sold or activated the gift card,other customers waiting in line
outcomes: The woman does not receive money from me
The hospital bill remains unpaid today
The child continues to suffer from a severe illness
My colleague keeps the money in the wallet
